S1.reason: The waveform rises smoothly to a peak around 0.125 s and fades out by 0.34 s, with no impulse at the start and a single onset. That is the shape of a swing's whoosh, and the harness classes it as a swing. One doubt: it sounds tonal and dark for a swish (see S3 and S4). It has no strike transient, so it is not mistaken for the hit sound. I cannot listen to it; this is judged from the picture and the features only.

S2.reason: It is 0.34 s long, with a 0.075 s attack, the peak at 0.125 s and T20 (the decay time) at 0.105 s. The tail fades cleanly with no lead-in silence. The class check flags nothing on the envelope, so it is within the range of Half-Life's own swing sounds.

S3.reason: The centroid (the average frequency of its energy) is 545 Hz, below the swing class's range of 608 to 912 Hz. 66.4% of the energy sits in 150-600 Hz, and almost none is above 2 kHz (2k-5k 0.6%, >5k 0.2%). The spectrogram agrees: the energy is concentrated in the lower half and the top rows are nearly empty. It needs more energy from 600 to 5000 Hz to have the airy swish of a swing.

S4.reason: The single onset is right for a swing. But flatness is 0.013, below the class's range of 0.03 to 0.13, so the sound is too pure where a swing should be broadband noise. It will read more like a low hum or rumble than a swish of air. Neither the picture nor the features show a pitch or band sweep through the swing.

S5.reason: The file is under the name the game looks for, sound/weapons/cbar_miss1.wav. It has no clipping (clipped 0), no DC offset (dc 0), and the peak is at -5 dBFS.
